diagnostic_thought_process: My previous analysis hypothesized that an NVIDIA driver mismatch was causing epilog script failures and draining the compute nodes. The newly executed commands confirm this hypothesis. The `grep` command on the controller revealed the `slurmd` log file name is templated with the node name (`slurmd-%n.log`), explaining why the previous `tail` command failed. The `dpkg -l | grep -i nvidia` command on the compute node provided the smoking gun, showing a mix of `570.x` and `580.x` NVIDIA packages, which directly corroborates the `Version mismatch` error seen in `dmesg`. The `journalctl` command for `slurmd` returned no entries, indicating logs are written to file, not the journal. Although I couldn't view the `gpu-test` script due to permissions, its presence as an epilog is confirmed in the blueprint, and its failure is the logical consequence of the unstable driver state.
potential_root_cause_with_reason: The deployment has failed because all Slurm compute nodes (`a3hspeed04-a3nodeset-0`, `a3hspeed04-a3nodeset-1`) are in a `DRAIN` state, preventing any jobs from running. The root cause is a broken NVIDIA driver installation on the compute nodes, where conflicting versions of driver packages were installed. Specifically, packages from the `570-server` series (e.g., `nvidia-dkms-570-server-open`) and the `580-server` series (e.g., `libnvidia-compute-580-server`) are present simultaneously. This created a version mismatch between the loaded kernel module and user-space libraries, as explicitly logged in `dmesg`. This conflict led to severe system instability, evidenced by a `general protection fault` in `tcpgpudmarxd` (a GPU Direct component). When a test job completed, the mandatory `gpu-test` epilog script failed due to the unstable driver, causing `slurmctld` to drain the nodes as a safety precaution.
